_purpose: Room 4D — Project 001, D-001B (Phase 1 + Phase 2). Groups of questions that test the same or overlapping knowledge, detected during import across all 5 sources (S001-S005). Duplicates are never deleted — grouping them preserves the signal that a repeated concept may indicate exam importance. Per the Phase 2 task brief, S001 and S002 contain substantial overlap (46 near-verbatim exact duplicates alone).

groups.reason: Both questions share the identical stem "From the choices below select the one which is false about Social Security (OASDHI):" and three of four answer choices are worded identically (or near-identically) across the two versions. Each version's distinct choice ('fully funded' vs. 'benefits closely match contributions') is marked as the false statement in its own version - two different printed variants of the same stock exam question testing the same underlying false-statement-about-OASDHI concept.
Same underlying fact (a policy premium is insurer revenue, not an insurer expense); reworded stem and choice 2 ("premiums" vs. "policy premiums").
Identical stem and choices ("What rule is used to determine the importance of a representation?").
Same moral-vs-morale-hazard concept tested in the reverse direction: given the term pick its definition (S004) vs. given the effect name the term (S003).
Identical stem and choices ("Which of the following statements regarding risk is TRUE?").
Both test which fact is/is not a true contract requirement, with different distractor sets and framing (IS-a-requirement vs. EXCEPT), but both agree "equal consideration" is not actually required.

All three test "required contents of a policy" with different distractor sets; Q-S004-033 is a byte-identical repeat of Q-S003-005 specifically, while Q-S004-006 is a conceptually-related variant with a different distractor set ("financial rating of the insurer" as the exception).
Same choices; minor stem wording difference ("California Fair Claims Settlement Practices resolution" vs. "...Regulations").
Identical stem and choices ("Who are members of the Medical Information Bureau?").
Identical stem and choices (Commissioner's actions after a revoked certificate of authority).

The "indemnity principle" tested 7 different ways across S003/S004 (contract-that-restores-to-pre-loss-position, vocabulary definition of "indemnity", the loss-cap rule, the formal contract-of-indemnity definition, "making whole" restated, and the insurance-policy-as-indemnity-contract definition). Within this cluster, Q-S003-038 and Q-S004-025 are byte-identical to each other. Repetition across 7 variants is a strong signal of exam importance.
